# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial — Bunion Surgery (Hallux Valgus), CPT 28296**
**Member:** Jordan Kimura
**Member ID:** W450262274
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice (Commercial/ACA), Maryland
**Denial Date:** 2026-08-25
**Reference Number:** POC-9297E0E467-45895
**Governing Policy:** Utilization Management (UM) Criteria (effective July 2026), MedStar Family Choice — https://www.medstarfamilychoicemd.com/-/media/project/mho/mfc/maryland-healthchoice-physicians/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115-utilization-management-um-criteria-july-2026.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which was denied on 2026-08-25 with the stated reason that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am asking MedStar Family Choice to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I believe the record supports that conclusion.

## Why I believe this decision should be reconsidered

The Utilization Management (UM) Criteria policy states that "MedStar Family Choice follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making," and that "MFC pre-authorization decisions are based on the following criteria:". However, the denial notice I received does not identify which specific clinical measurements, thresholds, or imaging standards were used to conclude that my imaging did not support medical necessity. Without that information, I am not able to see how my own records were measured against the plan's actual criteria.

What I can state plainly is what my records show:

- Weight-bearing foot radiographs taken 2026-07-26 documented a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- I have had 18 months of progressive foot pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 8 weeks of conservative care (2026-05-19 to 2026-07-14), including 20 physical therapy visits, activity modification, a wide toe-box shoe, and a custom orthotic, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-07 gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.
- On exam, I have positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side, cannot tolerate closed shoes, and am at risk of skin ulceration over the bony prominence.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

The policy also states that "Upon review for medical necessity, requests for ongoing services or treatment that have not demonstrated improvement in condition or benefit to the member will be subject to denial as not medically necessary." My records show the opposite pattern: I completed a full course of conservative treatment (physical therapy, orthotics, medication, and injection) and did not achieve lasting improvement, which is why my surgeon has recommended surgical correction.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

The policy states that "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request," and that a member or provider may contact the plan "to request specific utilization management criteria or to speak with a Medical Director... at 800-905-1722 or 410-933-2200 option 2, then option 1." I am formally making that request here, in writing.

I understand that MedStar Family Choice may use InterQual criteria, which is licensed clinical review software rather than a document available to the public. I have a right to see the specific criteria used to review my case. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, the plan must provide me, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on for this denial. I am requesting the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, so that I and my surgeon can respond directly to whatever standard was used.

## What I am asking for

I am asking MedStar Family Choice to:

1. Reconsider and reverse the denial of CPT 28296 for bunion surgery (hallux valgus) based on the clinical record described above; and
2. Provide, in writing, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and criteria text (or other documented UM criteria) applied to my case, as described above.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-21. I will send this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is not available, to the address I obtain by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.

Please contact me if you need any additional information from me or from Dr. Marchetti's office to complete this review.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Jordan Kimura
Member ID: W450262274
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
